title: herbctl
description: The herbstluftwm keybind imperatives: every composite mod- binding as a get-* verb - the float-layer state machines, the zoom register, the navigation chains - compiled to a standalone bunli binary.

content.heading: herbctl - the keybind imperatives, as a native binary
content: herbctl owns what the keybinds used to express as inline herbstluftwm chains: one verb per mod-key binding, each a faithful port of the tuned chain (or state machine) it replaces - compiled to a standalone executable with Bun and bunli, so the keybinds spawn binaries, not scripts.

content.heading: The verbs
content: Named for what they fetch, not for the key that triggers them:

get-south (mod-s) - the zoom/peek grid: urgent first (gated on the tag's urgent count), frame-down focus, the floating-layer branch (focus the layer and un-float via the tag's focused_client - the alias resolves stale mid-chain), cycle and pseudotile fallbacks.
get-forward (mod-w), get-shuffle (mod-shift-w) - leave-float and cycle-up; the shift ladder ends in a frame-tree rotate.
get-deck (mod-d), get-dedeck (mod-shift-d) - layout cyclers gated on frame occupancy; dedeck collapses to remove.
get-explore (mod-e), get-advice (mod-a) - explode/cycle and frame-focus-or-split pairs.
get-quiet (mod-q), get-hold (mod-shift-q), get-wrench (mod-ctrl-q) - the close/quit family: floats only un-float, empty frames collapse, xkill for the stubborn.
get-tuck (mod-shift-t) - the frame half of split-auto: the dots keybind chains it with the terminal spawn so the split only happens for a window that actually arrives.
get-vex/get-bend (mod-v/mod-b) and get-vexi/get-bendi (mod-ctrl-v/mod-ctrl-b) - the split-into-direction family.
get-hush (mod-shift-f) - fullscreen toggle; get-nap (mod-shift-z) - minimize toggle.

content.heading: The state machines
content: Three bindings carry whole register machines, ported branch for branch with the dots scripts as the contract:
get-zoom (mod-ctrl-f, the hc_zoom port) - press-count register: tile the float, maximize onto a dedicated <tag>-max tag (state recorded in hlwm env, a per-tag janitor daemon tidies up), restore.

get-extracted (mod-x, the hc_floatx port) - the layer-yank machine: focus a float and un-float it, yank the focused window into the float session (the vacated frame is never closed), defer to the tiling layer, drop a float back into an empty frame, and the no-floats tidying branch.
get-focus (mod-f, the hc_focus port) - the quick float toggle: no focus chasing, the register handled by hlwm itself.
Every branch is pinned by tests that mock the herbstclient binary and assert the exact command argv - no live WM is ever touched by the suite.
